clue.text: A couple of pairs any clever person should be able to put tog ether

definitions.text: A couple of pairs any clever person should be able to put tog ether

parts.words: A couple of pairs any clever person should be able to put tog ether
parts.note: two pairs of numbers, joined as in the idiom for working something out from obvious clues

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's hint that any bright person can assemble a couple of pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'put x and x together' means drawing the obvious conclusion; the clue describes the phrase itself. The page splits 'together' across a line break.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom about deducing the obvious names the two pairs being added up.

clue.text: The middle man pronounces it as waste

indicators.note: the clue tells us how the word is said, so a soundalike spelling is wanted

parts.note: rubbish or squandering, the word heard

explanation.surface: Someone in an intermediary role explains how he says a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The middle man' looks like a go-between, but it is the middle part of a man's body.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrow part of the human torso between ribs and hips is the body's middle.

clue.text: The sort of effort with which no one is at home

definitions.meaning: every member of the household has gone away

explanation.surface: A kind of effort made when the house stands empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A total effort is described with this phrase, and a house where every resident has left is said to be in this state.

clue.text: Order posted by a tyrant

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new order signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A command sent out by an autocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command, but it is an instruction to rearrange POSTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler who wields power cruelly is a synonym for a tyrant.

clue.text: Mass nourishment, although only a lightsnack

definitions.text: Mass nourishment, although only a lightsnack

parts.words: Mass nourishment, although only a lightsnack
parts.note: the thin bread given at Holy Communion is food at the Mass yet barely a mouthful

explanation.surface: Food for a crowd that is nevertheless just a nibble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests large quantities, but it is the Catholic service, where communicants receive a thin disc of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin disc of unleavened bread at Communion feeds worshippers but is a very slight biscuit.

clue.text: Incontrovertible evidence provided by trial photograph taken from negative

parts.note: a proof is a trial print or test copy
a positive is a print made from a photographic negative

explanation.surface: Courtroom evidence produced by a test print developed from a negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusive demonstration that settles a question beyond doubt is undeniable evidence.

clue.text: Shelter a teacher who keeps his eye on the port

definitions.text: who keeps his eye on the port

parts.note: to harbour is to give shelter to
a schoolmaster, or master, is a teacher

explanation.surface: Giving refuge to a teacher who watches over the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: The official in charge of a port's moorings and shipping keeps watch over it.

clue.text: Military code supplied by correspondents at the front

definitions.meaning: the regulations governing an armed force

definitions.text: supplied by correspondents at the front
definitions.meaning: pieces written by war reporters at the battle line

explanation.surface: Army regulations delivered by reporters on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'articles' as newspaper pieces, written by war correspondents.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic regulations governing army discipline, and also the news pieces filed by war reporters.

clue.text: Anti-bugging telephone device for one who is on the rocks

definitions.meaning: a gadget that garbles a phone signal so eavesdroppers cannot follow it

definitions.text: one who is on the rocks
definitions.meaning: a person clambering over rocks, scrambling up them

explanation.surface: A secure phone gadget for someone whose life has hit the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' suggests ruin or iced drinks; here it is a climber clambering over rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A device garbling phone signals, and a person who clambers over rough ground.

clue.text: The rack may well be needed by one already crippled by it

definitions.meaning: a torture device that pulls its victim's limbs

definitions.text: may well be needed by one already crippled by it
definitions.meaning: a litter for carrying a person who is too injured to walk

explanation.surface: A torture victim, already broken by the rack, needs more of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The word names both the rack, an instrument that stretches, and the litter used to carry the injured.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack for stretching is one sense; a litter for carrying casualties is the other.

clue.text: Credit frequently gets a smallholding

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Regular borrowing finances a small farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A CROFT is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rented farm, especially in Scotland, is a smallholding.

clue.text: Steal back to find a man of steel

parts.note: to rob is to steal

indicators.note: the word placed before it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A thief returns to find Superman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical automaton built of metal is a man made of steel.

clue.text: Country in which only the wealthy can afford to live

definitions.text: in which only the wealthy can afford to live
definitions.meaning: pomp and luxury, as in the phrase living in grand style

explanation.surface: A nation so expensive only the rich can reside there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Living in state' means living in grand luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is one sense; ceremonial grandeur, as in 'living in state', is the other.

clue.text: The deadly sin which originated in the jungles of America

definitions.meaning: idleness, one of the seven deadly sins

definitions.text: which originated in the jungles of America
definitions.meaning: a slow tree-dwelling mammal of Central and South American forests

explanation.surface: A deadly sin whose origins lie in American jungles.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness is one of the seven deadly sins, and a slow tree mammal shares its name.

clue.text: Silver is the first payment for grazing cattle

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for a verb meaning to take in livestock to graze for payment

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
the first is 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Silver was the earliest form of payment for pasturing cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. AGIST is an old legal verb: to take in another's livestock to graze for a fee, so the definition is loose in part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means pasturing another person's livestock for a fee, the source of such charges.

clue.text: Current escape device astronauts look down on

definitions.meaning: an electrical connection carrying stray current safely to ground

explanation.surface: An emergency exit that space crews gaze down at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day', but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire sending electricity safely to ground, and the planet that spacefarers see below them.

clue.text: The charm of a soft chime

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: The delight of a quietly ringing bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractiveness or allure is a synonym for charm.

clue.text: Charge to employ after getting a double century

indicators.note: the word for employ is placed after the letters for a and the double century
a double of the century means its letter is written twice

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A batsman is billed to play after scoring two hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a fee; it is a verb, to accuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally allege wrongdoing against someone is to charge them.

clue.text: In the middle of a cultivated rose one finds willow

indicators.note: the letter for one is set in the centre of the other letters
a cultivated plant is worked on, so the letters of rose are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a willow at the heart of a grown rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges ROSE to OSER, and 'In the middle of' puts I inside to give OSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliant willow used for basket-making is a kind of willow.

clue.text: Hound set to go after men of degree

indicators.note: the word set is placed after the letters for the graduates

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates

explanation.surface: A dog is set to chase university graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged scent dog is a breed of hound.

clue.text: Scotsman follows sailor on the road

indicators.note: the Scotsman's word comes after the sailor's in the answer

parts.note: tar is an old nickname for a sailor
Mac is a nickname for a Scot, from the Gaelic prefix of surnames

explanation.surface: A Scot trails a seaman along the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt surfacing is what roads are paved with, so it stands for the road itself.

clue.text: Drink down this!

parts.note: recalls the toast said before downing a drink, naming the opening the drink goes through

explanation.surface: A drinking toast urging someone to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The toast 'Down the ...!' names the mouth as an opening, like the trapdoor on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The drinking toast speaks of the throat as an opening in a ship's deck.

clue.text: A piece of poetry not in favour

parts.note: a verse is a stanza or piece of poetry

explanation.surface: A poem that is not favourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something means not being in favour of it.

clue.text: Sort of paper used for copying and for dating old clay tablets

definitions.text: Sort of paper used for copying

definitions.meaning: the radioactive method used to date ancient finds

explanation.surface: Paper for copies that also helps archaeologists date tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy paper coated with ink, and the element whose isotope is used for radiometric dating.

clue.text: Actor who hopes for another run?

definitions.text: Actor who hopes for another run?

parts.words: Actor who hopes for another run?
parts.note: a crowd player in films, and also a cricket run scored without the bat

explanation.surface: A performer hoping a show will be revived.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'run' suggests a show's season; here it is also an additional run in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A background film player, and an additional run in cricket.

clue.text: Eminent artist upped and made a dash for Scottish isle

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
ran is made a dash

explanation.surface: A distinguished painter got up and rushed off to a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' turns RA into AR. ARRAN is an island in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: An island in the Firth of Clyde is a Scottish isle.

clue.text: It may be called for as the situation changes

indicators.note: when a situation changes things are rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Something needed as circumstances shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation changes' rearranges AS THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is what is demanded when urgency arises, so it may be called for.

clue.text: An anchor chain running through it makes a hoarse sound

definitions.text: An anchor chain running through it

indicators.note: the clue says the word makes a certain sound, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: rough-voiced, the word heard

explanation.surface: An anchor chain grating through its hole makes a rasping noise.
explanation.walkthrough: A HAWSE is the hole in a ship's bow through which the anchor cable runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The bow opening on a ship through which the cable passes.

clue.text: Where the City man carries his umbrella and his hat if a cricketer

parts.words: Where the City man carries his umbrella
parts.note: a London businessman hangs his umbrella over his arm
a bowler is the hard round hat of a City gent

explanation.surface: A City gent with brolly and hat could pass for a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose workers once wore bowler hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who delivers the ball with the arm raised above the shoulder is a cricketer.

clue.text: Detained foreigners seen- returning to bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: the word seen is read backwards

explanation.surface: Interned aliens seen going back to bury someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SEEN into NEES.
explanation.definitionFit: People confined in wartime, especially enemy aliens, are detained foreigners.
